orientation: A six-case mechanical baseline found schema-constrained JSON editing parsed, applied, and finalized successfully in all cases, so fine-tuning was not justified. The run mostly produced final buffers rather than real edit operations, so it does not show that iterative editing improves writing or generalizes reliably.
finding: Schema-constrained decoding cleared the frozen mechanical reliability gate, supporting continued interface testing with the existing model rather than fine-tuning.
limitations: The corpus contained only six cases and one deterministic run.
Successful outputs mostly supplied final buffers instead of exercising append, replace, or delete transitions.
negative_evidence: The unconstrained arm failed one case by not finalizing the document.
The experiment established protocol reliability, not revision value or writing quality.
evidence_quotes: The schema-constrained arm completed all six cases.
This is not evidence that iterative editing improves writing.
The six-case corpus is intentionally small. A single deterministic run cannot establish general reliability, compare semantic quality, or support a model training decision.
